children.translated_text: The entire variety of forms of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) is rooted in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) —

children.text: jñātum vaktuṃ hantuṃ kaḥ śakto 'nyatra sarvajñāt // KAvk_75.1 //
children.translated_text: who is capable of knowing, speaking of, or destroying it, other than the Omniscient One?

children.text: śrāvastyāṃ svastimān pūrvaṃ jino jetavane sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in former times, the Victorious One, the all-seeing Blessed One, dwelling in <s>Jetavana</s>,
addressed the community of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks):
"Listen, for your welfare, O you whose minds are purified by the light of knowledge —
I shall tell you of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising) in its proper order.
This very latent impression of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the fashioner of the root-bondage
of the great mass of suffering, the poison-tree of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Conditioned by that are <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations), consisting of body, speech, and mind;
and arising from <s>saṃskāras</s> is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), consisting of the mind and the six sense-faculties.
Conditioned by that is <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), denoting perception and appearance;
and the locus of the mind and the six sense-faculties is <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense-bases), arising therefrom.
The conjunction of the six sense-bases is called <s>sparśa</s> (contact);

children.text: ṣaṭsparśānubhavo yaś ca vedanā sā prakīrtitā // KAvk_75.7 //
children.translated_text: and the experience of the six contacts is proclaimed as <s>vedanā</s> (feeling).
From that, through the passion of defilement toward sense-objects, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is born;
arising from that, <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) proceeds toward objects of desire and the like.
<s>Bhava</s> (becoming), arising from <s>upādāna</s>, consists of the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm;
<s>jāti</s> (birth), arising from <s>bhava</s>, revolves through various wombs and modes of birth.
The continuity of old age, death, sorrow, and the rest depends on <s>jāti</s>;
through the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> and the rest, there is the gradual cessation of all these.
This <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising) has many courses, its steps made by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) —
it should be contemplated by you who find peace and rest in the solitary forest.

children.text: parijñātaḥ samyag vrajati kila kālena tanutāṃ
children.translated_text: When rightly understood, it becomes attenuated in time;

children.text: tanutvaṃ saṃprāptaḥ sukhataranivāryaś ca bhavati // KAvk_75.11 //
children.translated_text: and having become attenuated, it is more easily overcome."

body.text:
iti kṣemendraviracitāyāṃ bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatāyāṃ
pratītyasamutpādāvadānaṃ pañcasaptatitamaḥ pallavaḥ |
body.translated_text:
Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā</s> composed by <s>Kṣemendra</s>,
the <s>Pratītyasamutpādāvadāna</s> (Story of Dependent Arising) is the seventy-fifth chapter.
